title: The Urgent Fraud Department Call
learningObjectives: Bank officials will never ask for your one-time password (OTP) or UPI PIN
Recognize false urgency threats such as immediate account freezing
Always disconnect and initiate contact through verified phone numbers on your card
startingContext: You receive an urgent phone call from 'Officer Mehta, Surya National Bank fraud desk' (fictional bank) claiming a suspicious ₹24,000 debit was attempted on your card.

redFlags.label: Unsolicited caller-initiated panic about suspicious debit
redFlags.explanation: Scammers manufacture high-stakes panic to make victims vulnerable and compliant.

redFlags.label: Authority intimidation and 15-minute account freeze threat
redFlags.explanation: Threatening sudden account lockouts forces victims into immediate action without thinking.

redFlags.label: Caller requesting one-time password or PIN code
redFlags.explanation: Authentic bank representatives never request passwords, OTPs, or secret credentials.

redFlags.label: Instruction to stay on the line and tell nobody
redFlags.explanation: Isolating the victim prevents second opinions from friends, relatives, or true bank staff.

messageOrEvent.speaker: Officer Mehta (fictional)
messageOrEvent.text: This is Surya National Bank security division. An unauthorized debit of ₹24,000 is pending on your card. We must verify your identity within 15 minutes or your account will be permanently frozen.

feedback.safeAlternative: Hang up immediately. Contact the official customer care number printed on the back of your card.
feedback.considerNext: Never verify account details over unsolicited incoming calls.

choices.label: Answer questions and confirm my details

explanation.whatHappened: You stayed on the line and began sharing personal verification details.
explanation.why: Engaging with caller identity checks hands sensitive data to potential impersonators.

choices.label: I'll hang up and call the number on my card / official app

explanation.whatHappened: You hung up and chose to call back via the verified number printed on your card.
explanation.why: Inbound calls can be spoofed; only numbers from official documents can be trusted.

explanation.whatHappened: You hung up the call immediately without verifying.
explanation.why: Ending the call stops manipulation, though checking your bank app is recommended to confirm safety.

messageOrEvent.speaker: Officer Mehta (fictional)
messageOrEvent.text: An SMS arrives with code ●●●●●●. Caller says: 'Read that 6-digit cancellation code to me immediately to stop the debit. Stay on the line, do not talk to anyone else!'

feedback.safeAlternative: Never speak or share OTP codes with anyone. Bank SMS explicitly states never to share OTP.
feedback.considerNext: Any caller asking for an OTP is attempting an unauthorized transaction.

explanation.whatHappened: You spoke the one-time code to the caller.
explanation.why: Sharing the code authorizes the attacker's transfer, resulting in immediate financial loss.

choices.label: Refuse to share the OTP and end the call

explanation.whatHappened: You refused to divulge the code and disconnected the call.
explanation.why: Holding onto your one-time passwords prevents unauthorized account access.

choices.label: Say I'll call back after speaking to family

explanation.whatHappened: You broke the psychological isolation tactic by seeking outside advice.
explanation.why: Consulting trusted persons breaks the pressure barrier created by scammers.

messageOrEvent.speaker: Surya National Bank Helpline (fictional)
messageOrEvent.text: Official support confirms: 'We have not attempted any debit, and bank representatives never ask for OTPs or PINs over the phone.'

feedback.safeAlternative: Dial the national cyber helpline 1930 or submit details on the official reporting portal.
feedback.considerNext: Reporting scam calls helps authorities disable fraudulent numbers.

explanation.whatHappened: You reported the fraudulent caller to the official cyber fraud helpline.
explanation.why: Prompt reporting helps track down impersonation syndicates.

explanation.whatHappened: You blocked the caller number on your device.
explanation.why: Blocking protects your device from repeat calls, though reporting helps others.

messageOrEvent.text: Your account was compromised by sharing the verification code.

outcome.title: Account Compromised by Disclosing OTP
outcome.text: In this simulation, that choice would have cost you ₹24,000. Sharing the OTP allowed the impersonator to authorize a real transfer out of your account. No real money moved.

messageOrEvent.text: Impersonation fraud thwarted and reported to cybercrime authorities.

outcome.title: Impersonator Thwarted and Reported
outcome.text: You recognized that genuine bank staff never ask for OTPs or PINs. You hung up, confirmed safety with official support, and reported the attempt.

outcome.title: Call Terminated Safely
outcome.text: You did not disclose credentials to the caller and avoided financial loss.

outcome.title: Immediate Disconnect
outcome.text: You refused to engage with high-pressure caller intimidation.

recommendedSafeActions: Never disclose one-time passwords, UPI PINs, or card CVVs to any caller
Disconnect suspicious calls and reach out via the official customer support number on your debit card
Report suspicious numbers directly to national fraud reporting lines such as 1930
learningSummary: Impersonation scams thrive on creating fear of sudden loss. True financial institutions will never call to demand that you read aloud an OTP to cancel a transaction.
